content.text: Confirmed: the two tests assert mutually exclusive outcomes for the same input, so no `src/lib.rs` implementation can make both pass. Reporting this as the outcome.

findings.summary: spaces_become_hyphens and spaces_become_underscores both call slugify("Hello World") but assert different, mutually exclusive expected outputs ("hello-world" vs "hello_world"), so no single implementation of slugify in src/lib.rs can satisfy both tests simultaneously.
findings.failure_scenario: For any deterministic slugify(title: &str) -> String, slugify("Hello World") produces exactly one string. If it returns "hello-world", spaces_become_underscores fails; if it returns "hello_world", spaces_become_hyphens fails. cargo test confirms: with the current hyphen-based implementation, spaces_become_underscores fails with left: "hello-world", right: "hello_world". This is a task requirement conflict, not a bug fixable via src/lib.rs alone — tests/slug.rs itself must change (not permitted) for both to pass.
